course_info.faculty: Faculty of Engineering and Natural Sciences

catalog_course_description: Sequences and series. Power series. Taylor polynomials, Taylor series and approximation. Visualizing functions of several variables; graphs and contour diagrams. Vectors. Differentation in several variables; partial and directional derivatives. Linear and quadratic approxiamtion. Classification of local extrema. Optimization, Lagrange Multipliers. Integration in several variables. Iterated integrals. Change of variables; polar, cylindrical and spherical coordinates.
course_learning_outcomes: Define the notion of convergence of series and use various tests to determine series convergence
Find Taylor representations of functions and approximate functions via Taylor polynomials
Understand and use the concept of a function of several variables, draw graphs in 3-space
Use the properties of vectors and operations with vectors
Compute partial derivatives, directional derivatives and write equations of tangent planes to surfaces
Apply partial derivatives to find and test local extrema
Evaluate double integrals in Cartesian and polar coordinates and triple integrals in Cartesian coordinates
course_objective: To introduce series and concepts of multivariable calculus, to relate notions in multivariable calculus to their analogues in single variable.

resources: Textbook: Calculus Early Transcendentals 2nd Edition (Global Edition), Briggs, Cochran & Gillett.
